subject: Latency spike on M6-rc1 — request for rapid revert & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@novapay.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T08:14:22-07:00
Subject: High P95 latencies since M6-rc1 rollout to nova-pay-prod pool

Alex —

We pushed your M6-rc1 image to our dedicated nova-pay-prod pool at 03:30 PT last night as part of the scheduled blackout window. Since ~04:10 PT we’re seeing a sharp P95 jump across payment-intent endpoints: historically ~220-320ms, now 950-1,200ms. This is directly causing checkout timeouts for ~2% of sessions and increased tokenization retries. Attached is a short CSV with the 5min buckets.

Can you escalate on your side? We need either a hotfix or an immediate revert to the previous M5-stable image. This is impacting peak traffic and business KPIs.

Thanks —
Sam
Sam Lee
SRE Lead, NovaPay
ops@novapay.com

Subject: Re: High P95 latencies since M6-rc1 rollout to nova-pay-prod pool

Sam — thank you for the signal and the CSV. I’m escalating internally now.

Short summary for transparency: NovaPay observed P95 ~1s after M6-rc1 promotion to nova-pay-prod pool. Impact: checkout timeouts for ~2% of sessions.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Authorization to perform a canary revert of the nova-pay-prod pool to M5-stable (we expect <5 minutes to flip the canary, full roll for the pool ~13 minutes with graceful drain).
- If revert is required, permission to apply a one-time SLA credit (we will propose credit amount after I confirm scope).

Looping in Vivek for rollback plan and Marissa for customer comms. Laura for any contractual/partial-credit approvals you may need to sign off.

I’ll follow up in ~10–15 minutes with a proposed runbook.

—Alex

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-12T08:41:37-07:00
Subject: RE: High P95 latencies since M6-rc1 rollout to nova-pay-prod pool

Alex/Team —

Thanks for the ping; I’ve pulled the traces and perf profiles from nova-pay-prod canary nodes. Quick notes:
- Root cause hypothesis: M6-rc1 introduced a change in kv-cache sharding plus a spacing variance in the attention kernel that increases tail latency under the payment-intent request shape (short prompts, high concurrency).
- Observed: p95 spike correlates with KV-cache miss rate increase and more frequent context window recompute.

Suggested immediate action (canary-first):
1) Revert canary nodes in nova-pay-prod to M5-stable (image tag m5-stable-20261014). Canary flip should be <5 minutes; we validate p95 on the canary for 15 minutes.
2) If canary resolves p95 to baseline, roll revert across the remaining nodes in staged batch with health checks and traffic split; expected full pool reversion ~13 minutes with rolling drain.
3) While reverting, enable KV-cache aggressive prefetch heuristic (removes some mem-savings but should cut misses) as a short-term mitigation if we see revert delay.
4) Post-mortem: collect KV miss histograms, attention kernel counters, request shapes.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Revert will restore baseline cost profile; if we can’t revert, the fallback is to pin NovaPay to M5-stable for 7 days (we’ll coordinate billing adjustments).
- Canary revert requires permission to modify NovaPay’s dedicated pool images; confirm authorization.

I’ve attached a short playbook we use for canary reverts. If you approve, I can kick the canary revert immediately and monitor.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Head of Inference Engineering, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachment: m6-revert-playbook.pdf (PDF, 64KB)

- 09:10 PT: Confirming we are starting a canary revert; provide expected window and what to expect (no config changes, just image revert).
- 09:30 PT: Confirm canary validation results or escalate to immediate full rollback.
- 10:00 PT: Post-rollback update and options for temporary SLA remediation.

I’ll use the template for partial credit offers (we typically propose a 10–30% usage credit tier for P95 breaches depending on duration). I’ll capture NovaPay’s preference in the ticket.

—Marissa
